title: Chapter 2: Walking the Beaten Path Together 7
content: Now that the self-introductions and sword replenishments are done, let's get out of here quickly.
"Are you feeling alright?"
Just as I was thinking that, Erika continued the conversation.
"Yes, thanks to you, I was able to receive treatment without any issues."
"What? Shara, you got hurt?"
Teppe's surprised voice made Shara nod.
"Yes, I was attacked by three Golden Ogres while on my way to treat an injured villager."
"How did you manage to come out unscathed?!"
"Yes, I was saved by the Longdagger couple over there."
Teppe paused for a moment, deep in thought.
"You defeated three Golden Ogres with just the two of you?"
He asked hesitantly, and when I nodded, Teppe buried his face in his hands and looked up at the ceiling.
"Darn it! I should have charged more!"
What an honest person. Honestly, I wonder if he’s not cut out for this business?
No, he’s probably aware of his shortcomings, which is why he’s resorting to this unique selling method.
I began to understand a lot more.
Shara knew about the request from the girl because she was called to the village to treat that father. The Church and the Adventurer Guild have a good relationship, both claiming to protect the weak.
I’d rather not become too well-known, as that might lead to designated requests from the Church.
"By the way, do you have any business here?"
Erika glanced at the paper bag on the counter and asked.
Oh, good, this could lead to us leaving this place.
It’s a way of saying we shouldn’t interrupt your business.
"That’s right, Teppe."
Shara turned her body towards Teppe.
Good, this will allow us to slip out of the store casually.
"I brought the repair items you requested for the orphanage."
The moment I heard the word "orphanage," I realized my plans had crumbled.
"The orphanage...?"
Erika murmured, asking.
Ah, I see how it is.
I kept my expression neutral, trying not to look too distant.
The Solnzali family has a title.
Generally, titles are attached to individuals, even among nobles and royalty.
For example, "The Judging King" Tullia Faltarl or "The Western Gale" Cortas Bambanir.
However, the Solnzali family is unique in that the title belongs to the family itself.
This is because the entire clan acts in a manner befitting that title as if it were a tradition.
The Solnzali family is known as "The Guardians of Orphans."
"Yes, Teppe is repairing the broken ironware for the orphanage free of charge."
"When the Church has a good relationship, they can receive work from the Church, you know."
Shara proudly answered Erika's question while boasting about her friend, but Teppe didn’t take it too well. Their easygoing exchange revealed their friendship; they were indeed close.
"What kind of place is that orphanage?"
Erika asked, clearly fidgeting with curiosity.
What is this strange passion the Solnzali family has for this orphanage?
It’s not uncommon for nobles to support orphanages, but the Solnzali family's involvement is said to go beyond the norm.
"It’s an orphanage run by the Adventurer Guild, and we, the Church, also help out."
The fact that the Adventurer Guild runs the orphanage is very much in line with the adventurer town of Hekatai.
In other towns, it’s common for the Church to operate them.
It’s rare to find a town with so many adventurers, where death is a daily occurrence, so it’s not surprising that the Adventurer Guild runs the orphanage in Hekatai.
"Does that orphanage accept donations?"
While it might seem obvious that orphanages accept donations, some do not.
In cases where the orphanage is effectively run by nobles, the noble's face can be involved, leading to them not accepting donations.
Ordinary commoners wouldn’t know such things, so Erika's question was quite noble-like, but Shara didn’t seem to find it particularly odd.
"Of course, we accept donations from anyone at any time."
Would you like me to guide you there right now?
Shara’s suggestion was likely half a joke, but she chose the wrong person to say it to.
"I would love to, but we’re planning to check our equipment and hunt some suitable monsters."
When did that plan come about? I thought, but I certainly wanted to check our new gear sooner rather than later, so I had no objections.
"So, I’ll leave this with you, and could you deliver it to the orphanage?"

Saying that, Erika handed Shara a leather pouch filled with the money from selling the Golden Ogre's magic stones. Though she had spent quite a bit, there was still enough left in the pouch, which was heavy due to the gold coins inside.
"Eh?"
Shara, who naturally accepted the pouch thanks to Erika's fluid movements, let out a bewildered voice at its weight.
"Well then, we’ll take our leave. Please take care of the rest."
"Eh? Eh? Eh?"
Ignoring Shara, who was torn between the heavy pouch and Erika, Erika made her exit. Isn’t she a bit too free-spirited?
I felt sympathy for Shara, who looked more confused than anything.
"Well, take care on your way there."
I said to Shara, stifling a wry smile as I followed after Erika.
"I really did it this time."
Erika said seriously when I caught up to her.
"To donate all the money we earned without your permission, isn’t that a failure as a wife?"
The fact that she would consider donating that amount without hesitation is not something a normal person would do, so I thought her concerns were misplaced, but I shook my head.
"It’s not like we’re struggling for living expenses, and it suits you just fine."
"That’s not the point."
She seemed genuinely troubled, her expression unusually dark.
Could it be that she was feeling down?
It’s a comforting thought to realize that even Erika Solnzali can feel down at times.
Surely, that’s a side of her she doesn’t show to others.
"People have certain traits they can’t help, for better or worse. In your case, it just happens to align with the Solnzali family’s teachings."
I ignored her voice saying it’s not exactly a family teaching, as it seemed too weak to say anything.
"I find that aspect of you quite admirable."
For a brief moment, she seemed to want to say something, but Erika lowered her head and spoke.
"If you say so."
I nodded in satisfaction at her words.
I want Erika Solnzali to remain true to herself.
For that, I would spare no effort.
"By the way, I still don’t understand why you were completely unknown at the academy."
Erika said this about an hour after we left the town, considering hunting some monsters along the roadside since there were no suitable requests at the Adventurer Guild.
While I was feeling a fresh surprise at the weak monsters I had never seen in the Faltarl Kingdom, it felt more like a leisurely activity than a monster hunt.
Of course, to ordinary people, even those monsters are a significant threat, so I wouldn’t slack off.
"Because I’m the second son of a poor viscount."
I sat down in a suitable shade to take a break and eat some dried meat while saying this.
If I were to honestly say I attended the academy just to see your face and had no real motivation, I felt like I would get scolded, so I made up a reason.
"Is that really how it is?"
Erika tilted her head, as the daughter of a grand marquis family, her rank was different from mine.
It seemed my reasoning was too flimsy, and she looked doubtful.
"Also, I’m not good at magic, or rather, I can’t use it. So even if I get attention for my sword skills, it doesn’t mean much."
Erika looked at me in disbelief, asking how not being able to use magic would be a hindrance for me.
"So you were slacking off?"

No, she didn’t look disappointed; she looked dissatisfied. I thought it was unnecessary for her to look displeased over something from the past. But I kept quiet, as I felt I would get scolded if I spoke up.
"Besides, I was busy with my adventurer work, so I couldn’t focus on my studies."
"Even so, it’s frustrating that the man who becomes my husband was looked down upon."
At that time, you didn’t even remember my name, I thought, reminiscing about something that was quite recent yet felt nostalgic.
"Well, it’s all in the past now."
As I muttered something that wasn’t really an answer, Erika softened her expression and agreed.
I felt happy that Erika could smile when I talked about our academy days.
After all, just a little while ago, I had seen her continuously cursing in the carriage.
After that, we took a moment of silence to rest.
The new equipment was worth the price, and Erika was able to remain true to herself.
It was a good day.
"Yes, from now on, my husband should just show the world that he is extraordinary."
…It really is a good day.
For Erika Solnzali to expect something extraordinary from her husband seems natural for someone so full of talent.
But the problem is, that husband is me.
I’m not boasting, but I’m just a second son of a poor viscount.
I take pride in being slightly better than other students who only attended the academy because their master was excellent, but even so, I must pale in comparison to the top students.

Moreover, Eluza, my fellow disciple under the same master, was more talented than I was. This means my talent isn’t anything special. But if that’s what she wishes for, I intend to respond with all my might.
Even if this farce ends in a year.
On that day, when I gained a small goal for my future life, suddenly that goal was thwarted.
I might lose my home.
